text:
rachel: follow-up from the fairness postmortem — proposing a "session watermark" to protect steady low-volume customers from token-draining sessions. want quick opinions on interface and edge vs central enforcement

omar: tl;dr what is session watermark?

rachel: per-session soft cap expressed as a decreasing watermark. as session consumes tokens, watermark drops; if it crosses thresholds we either throttle, degrade, or switch model. unique from tenant credit which is per-account

peter: why per-session vs per-tenant? sounds like extra state

rachel: attacks were from long-running sessions that bypass tenant burst detectors. session watermark isolates that vector without penalizing other concurrent sessions under same tenant

kayla: enforcement location? edge or central?

omar: prefer hybrid. edge maintains ephemeral session watermarks with TTL; central keeps authoritative snapshot for reconciliation and long-tail analytics

rachel: exact plan: edge creates session entry on first request (session_id header). edge decrements watermark by tokens_suggested and marks provisional. central periodically reconciles and can emit a session override: drain/soft-degrade/confirm

peter: how do we avoid double-counting when user reconnects to a different edge?

kayla: session id should be globally unique (uuid) and included in signed auth token. edges fetch or create session with a small read-through cache from central store; if absent central initializes watermark

omar: what about memory pressure on edges? we only keep hot sessions (last-seen < 2m) and evict LRU. central is source-of-truth for long-lived sessions

rachel: penalty behavior: prefer graduated degrade path: 1) reduce allowed tokens/request, 2) if persists, route to cheaper variant, 3) last resort 429 with explanatory header

peter: telemetry needed: per-session token_total, token_rate, time_since_start, degrade_count, unify with tenant abuse_score. console should show heatmap of sessions by token tail

dev-bot: load-test summary: https://ci.company/perm/session-watermark/exp-7 90th percentile session-tail reduced by 33% in tests

kayla: race concern: two edges might read same watermark and both allow requests that together exceed watermark. mitigation?

omar: use a small provisional window combined with a central CAS when close to threshold. edges can over-allocate up to a buffer and central truncates future admits. buffer sized to cover network RTTs (200-400 tokens)

rachel: API UX: responses in JSON include {"session_status": "ok|soft_degraded|blocked", "session_remaining": "420"}. also add header X-Redwood-Session-Remaining for quick client-side checks

peter: backward compat: legacy clients ignore new fields. still return 429 on hard block. for soft_degrade we return 200 with reduced payload but include header X-Redwood-Soft-Degrade:1

kayla: testing matrix: session reconnects, multi-edge oversubscribe, cold cache on central, cross-tenant interference, and private deployment compliance (no session persistence outside customer VPC)

omar: rollout: shadow mode for 48h, then dedicated pilot tenants, then staged ramp for hosted. quick kill: have edge flag to ignore session watermarks and central switch to drain overrides

peter: curious about fairness scoring: how does session watermark interact with tenant-level quotas and global fairness?

rachel: scoring merge order: session constraints first, tenant credits second, global fairness last. session only restricts that individual session's share, tenant-level still enforces tenant budget across sessions

kayla: ops note: ensure audit logs write decision reason (session_degrade/tenant_throttle/global_fair) and retain per compliance retention config; private installs may require longer retention

dev-bot: created INFRA-1988: "session-watermark-rollout" with checklist link: https://infra-tracker/INFRA-1988/checklist

omar: one more safety: if central is unreachable, edges should fall back to conservative defaults (lower watermark) not permissive ones

rachel: agreed. default fallback is to halve provisional remaining tokens when central unreachable and signal degraded mode to client

peter: ok seems actionable. rachel please add the exact CAS semantics and eviction TTLs to the PR

rachel: will do, pushing PR with simulator and dashboard queries in 36h

kayla: great, ping when green and we'll schedule a rollout window

rachel: thanks all, closing thread for now
